content_sanskrit: अथ परिमलजामवाप्य लक्ष्मीमवयवदीपितमण्डनश्रियस्ताः । वसतिमभिविहाय रम्यहावाः सुरपतिसूनुविलोभनाय जग्मुः ॥
padaccheda: अथ । परिमलजाम् । अवाप्य । लक्ष्मीम् । अवयवदीपितमण्डनश्रियः । ताः । वसतिम् । अभिविहाय । रम्यहावाः । सुरपतिसूनुविलोभनाय । जग्मुः

meaning_english: Then, those celestial nymphs, possessing charming coquettish gestures and a beauty enhanced by their limbs that outshone their ornaments, having acquired a loveliness born of fragrance, left their dwelling and went forth to seduce Arjuna, the son of Indra.

content_sanskrit: द्रुतपदमभियातुमिच्छतीनां गमनपरिक्रमलाघवेन तासाम् । अवनिषु चरणैः पृथुस्तनीनामलघुनितम्बतया चिरं निषेदे ॥
padaccheda: द्रुतपदम् । अभियातुम् । इच्छतीनाम् । गमनपरिक्रमलाघवेन । तासाम् । अवनिषु । चरणैः । पृथुस्तनीनाम् । अलघुनितम्बतया । चिरम् । निषेदे

meaning_english: Although the full-breasted nymphs desired to walk quickly and possessed a natural swiftness in their gait, their feet lingered long on the ground due to the heaviness of their large hips.

content_sanskrit: निहितसरसयावकैर्बभासे चरणतलैः कृतपद्धतिर्वधूनाम् । अविरलविततेव शक्रगोपैररुणितनीलतृणोलपा धरित्री ॥

meaning_english: The earth, with paths marked by the feet of the nymphs which were adorned with fresh red lac-dye, shone as if it were a field of blue grass and reeds reddened by a dense swarm of Indragopa insects.

content_sanskrit: ध्वनिरगविवरेषु नूपुराणां पृथुरशनागुणशिञ्जितानुयातः । प्रतिरवविततो वनानि चक्रे मुखरसमुत्सुकहंससारसानि ॥

meaning_english: The sound of the nymphs' anklets, accompanied by the tinkling of their heavy girdles, spread through the mountain caves by echoes and made the forests resonant with the excited cries of swans and cranes.

content_sanskrit: अवचयपरिभोगवन्ति हिंस्रैः सहचरितान्यमृगाणि काननानि । अभिदधुरभितो मुनिं वधूभ्यः समुदितसाध्वसविक्लवं च चेतः ॥

meaning_english: The surrounding forests, though frequented by beasts of prey and devoid of gentle deer, were suitable for enjoyment and gathering flowers. This sight, along with their own minds agitated by rising fear, indicated the presence of the sage (Arjuna) to the celestial women.

content_sanskrit: नृपतिमुनिपरिग्रहेण सा भूः सुरसचिवाप्सरसां जहार चेतः । उपहितपरमप्रभावधाम्नां न हि जयिनां तपसामलङ्घ्यमस्ति ॥

meaning_english: That land, occupied by the royal sage Arjuna, captivated the minds of the Apsaras. Indeed, for the victorious who are abodes of supreme, inherent power, there is nothing that cannot be achieved by their austerities.

content_sanskrit: सचकितमिव विस्मयाकुलाभिः शुचिसिकतास्वतिमानुषाणि ताभिः । क्षितिषु ददृशिरे पदानि जिष्णोरुपहितकेतुरथाङ्गलाञ्छनानि ॥

meaning_english: Then, filled with wonder, the Apsaras saw on the pure, sandy grounds the superhuman footprints of Arjuna. Marked with the divine signs of the banner and the chariot-wheel, they gazed upon them as if with alarm.

content_sanskrit: अतिशयितवनान्तरद्युतीनां फलकुसुमावचयेऽपि तद्विधानाम् । ऋतुरिव तरुवीरुधां समृद्ध्या युवतिजनैर्जगृहे मुनिप्रभावः ॥

meaning_english: Even as the young women, whose own splendor surpassed that of the forest, were gathering fruits and flowers, the sage's power was perceived by them through the extraordinary abundance of the trees and creepers, just as one perceives the presence of a season.

content_sanskrit: मृदितकिसलयः सुराङ्गनानां ससलिलवल्कलभारभुग्नशाखः । बहुमतिमधिकां ययावशोकः परिजनतापि गुणाय सद्गुणानाम् ॥

meaning_english: An Ashoka tree, whose sprouts were crushed by the celestial women and whose branches were bent under the weight of their wet bark-garments, gained great esteem. Indeed, even servitude to the virtuous turns into an advantage.

content_sanskrit: यमनियमकृशीकृतस्थिराङ्गः परिददृशे विधृतायुधः स ताभिः । अनुपमशमदीप्ततागरीयान्कृतपदपङ्क्तिरथर्वणेव वेदः ॥

meaning_english: He (Arjuna) was seen by them. His firm body was emaciated by ascetic practices, yet he held his weapons. He was venerable due to the brilliance of his unparalleled tranquility, appearing like the Veda whose text was arranged by the sage Atharvan.

content_sanskrit: शशधर इव लोचनाभिरामैर्गगनविसारिभिरंशुभिः परीतः । शिखरनिचयमेकसानुसद्मा सकलमिवापि दधन्महीधरस्य ॥

meaning_english: Though dwelling on a single peak, he (Arjuna), surrounded by his lustre which was pleasing to the eyes and spread across the sky, seemed to bear the entire cluster of the mountain's peaks, just like the moon.

content_sanskrit: सुरसरिति परं तपोऽधिगच्छन्विधृतपिशङ्गबृहज्जटाकलापः । हविरिव विततः शिखासमूहैः समभिलषन्नुपवेदि जातवेदाः ॥

meaning_english: Practicing supreme austerity in the celestial river, wearing a large mass of tawny matted hair, he appeared like the sacrificial fire near the altar, which, desiring the oblation, spreads out with its mass of flames.

content_sanskrit: सदृशमतनुमाकृतेः प्रयत्नं तदनुगुणामपरैः क्रियामलङ्घ्याम् । दधदलघु तपः क्रियानुरूपं विजयवतीं च तपःसमां समृद्धिम् ॥

meaning_english: He possessed a great effort befitting his noble form, an unsurpassable action corresponding to that effort, a great austerity in keeping with his actions, and a victorious splendor equal to his austerity.

content_sanskrit: चिरनियमकृशोऽपि शैलसारः शमनिरतोऽपि दुरासदः प्रकृत्या । ससचिव इव निर्जनेऽपि तिष्ठन्मुनिरपि तुल्यरुचिस्त्रिलोकभर्तुः ॥

meaning_english: Though emaciated by long vows, he had the strength of a mountain. Though devoted to tranquility, he was by nature difficult to approach. Though in a solitary place, he seemed to be with his ministers. And though a sage, his splendor was equal to that of Indra, the lord of the three worlds.

content_sanskrit: तनुमवजितलोकसारधाम्नीं त्रिभुवनगुप्तिसहां विलोकयन्त्यः । अवययुरमरस्त्रियोऽस्य यत्नं विजयफले विफलं तपोधिकारे ॥

meaning_english: Beholding his body, which surpassed the essence of all worlds in lustre and was capable of protecting the three worlds, the celestial women inferred that their effort to disrupt his penance would be fruitless, as victory was its certain outcome.

content_sanskrit: मुनिदनुतनयान्विलोभ्य सद्यः प्रतनुबलान्यधितिष्ठतस्तपांसि । अलघुनि बहु मेनिरे च ताः स्वं कुलिशभृता विहितं पदे नियोगम् ॥

meaning_english: Having previously seduced sages and demons, thereby mastering their less potent austerities, the Apsaras now highly esteemed their own mission, ordained by Indra, in this important task concerning Arjuna, whose penance was far greater.

content_sanskrit: अथ कृतकविलोभनं विधित्सौ युवतिजने हरिसूनुदर्शनेन । प्रसभमवततार चित्तजन्मा हरति मनो मधुरा हि यौवनश्रीः ॥

meaning_english: Then, as the young women, upon seeing Arjuna, desired to enact their feigned seduction, the mind-born god of love (Kamadeva) forcibly descended upon them. Indeed, the sweet beauty of youth captivates the mind.

content_sanskrit: सपदि हरिसखैर्वधूनिदेशाद्ध्वनितमनोरमवल्लकीमृदङ्गैः । युगपद् ऋतुगणस्य संनिधानं वियति वने च यथायथं वितेने ॥

meaning_english: Immediately, at the command of the women, the Gandharvas, friends of Indra, playing their charming lutes and drums, simultaneously brought about the presence of all the seasons, each manifesting appropriately in the sky and the forest.

content_sanskrit: सजलजलधरं नभो विरेजे विवृतिमियाय रुचिस्तडिल्लतानाम् । व्यवहितरतिविग्रहैर्वितेने जलगुरुभिः स्तनितैर्दिगन्तरेषु ॥

meaning_english: The sky shone with water-laden clouds. The brilliance of the lightning-creepers became manifest. The sound of thunder, heavy with rain and known to interrupt the union of lovers, spread through all quarters of the sky.

content_sanskrit: परिसुरपतिसूनुधाम सद्यः समुपदधन्मुकुलानि मालतीनाम् । विरलमपजहार बद्धबिन्दुः सरजसतामवनेरपां निपातः ॥

meaning_english: Immediately causing Malati buds to appear around Arjuna's hermitage, a sparse shower of rain, forming distinct drops, removed the dustiness from the surface of the earth.

content_sanskrit: प्रतिदिशमभिगच्छताभिमृष्टः ककुभविकाससुगन्धिनानिलेन । नव इव विबभौ सचित्तजन्मा गतधृतिराकुलितश्च जीवलोकः ॥

meaning_english: Touched by the wind blowing in every direction, fragrant with the blossoming of Kakubha flowers, the world of living beings, with passions aroused, shone as if renewed, yet it also lost its composure and became agitated.

content_sanskrit: व्यथितमपि भृशं मनो हरन्ती परिणतजम्बुफलोपभोगहृष्टा । परभृतयुवतिः स्वनं वितेने नवनवयोजितकण्ठरागरम्यम् ॥

meaning_english: A young female cuckoo, delighted by eating ripe Jambu fruits, produced a song that was charming with its ever-new melody. Her song was so captivating that it could greatly enthrall even an afflicted mind.

content_sanskrit: अभिभवति मनः कदम्बवायौ मदमधुरे च शिखण्डिनां निनादे । जन इव न धृतेश्चचाल जिष्णुर्न हि महतां सुकरः समाधिभङ्गः ॥

meaning_english: Although the wind, fragrant with Kadamba flowers, and the sweet, passionate cries of the peacocks were overpowering the mind, Arjuna did not swerve from his resolve like an ordinary person. Indeed, breaking the concentration of the great-minded is not an easy task.

content_sanskrit: धृतबिसवलयावलिर्वहन्ती कुमुदवनैकदुकूलमात्तबाणा । शरदमलतले सरोजपाणौ घनसमयेन वधूरिवाललम्बे ॥

meaning_english: Autumn, personified as a bride, made her appearance. She wore bracelets of lotus stalks, a garment of water-lily groves, and held arrows of kasha flowers. Brought in by the rainy season, she rested upon the spotless earth, her hand being a lotus.

content_sanskrit: समदशिखिरुतानि हंसनादैः कुमुदवनानि कदम्बपुष्पवृष्ट्या । श्रियमतिशयिनीं समेत्य जग्मुर्गुणमहतां महते गुणाय योगः ॥

meaning_english: The cries of peacocks, joining with the calls of swans, and the water-lily groves, combining with showers of Kadamba flowers, attained an exceeding beauty. Indeed, the association of the great in virtue leads to even greater virtue.

content_sanskrit: सरजसमपहाय केतकीनां प्रसवमुपान्तिकनीपरेणुकीर्णम् । प्रियमधुरसनानि षट्पदाली मलिनयति स्म विनीलबन्धनानि ॥

meaning_english: A swarm of bees, abandoning the pollen-laden blossoms of the Ketaki flowers that were sprinkled with pollen from nearby Kadamba trees, began to soil the Bandhujiva flowers, which had very dark stalks and a juice that was dear and sweet to them.

content_sanskrit: मुकुलितमतिशय्य बन्धुजीवं धृतजलबिन्दुषु शाद्वलस्थलीषु । अविरलवपुषः सुरेन्द्रगोपा विकचपलाशचयश्रियं समीयुः ॥

meaning_english: On the green meadows holding drops of water, the densely packed Indragopa insects, surpassing the beauty of the budding Bandhujiva flowers, attained the splendor of a heap of full-blown Palasha flowers.

content_sanskrit: अविरलफलिनीवनप्रसूनः कुसुमितकुन्दसुगन्धिगन्धवाहः । गुणमसमयजं चिराय लेभे विरलतुषारकण्।अस्तुषारकालः ॥

meaning_english: The dewy season (Hemanta), characterized by sparse frost, abundant Priyangu flowers, and a breeze fragrant with jasmine, possessed for a long time a charm that was unseasonal, as these features are typically associated with other times of the year.

content_sanskrit: निचयिनि लवलीलताविकासे जनयति लोध्रसमीरणे च हर्षम् । विकृतिमुपययौ न पाण्डुसूनुश्चलति नयान्न जिगीषतां हि चेतः ॥

meaning_english: Even when the abundant blooming of Lavali creepers and the breeze from Lodhra trees were causing delight, the son of Pandu (Arjuna) did not undergo any mental agitation. For indeed, the mind of those who wish to conquer does not swerve from the path of policy.

content_sanskrit: कतिपयसहकारपुष्परम्यस्तनुतुहिनोऽल्पविनिद्रसिन्दुवारः । सुरभिमुखहिमागमान्तशंसी समुपययौ शिशिरः स्मरैकबन्धुः ॥

meaning_english: The winter season (Shishira) arrived, made lovely by a few mango blossoms, with light frost and few blossomed Sinduvara trees. Announcing the end of the cold season and the advent of spring, it was the sole friend of the god of love.

content_sanskrit: कुसुमनगवनान्युपैतुकामा किसलयिनीमवलम्ब्य चूतयष्टिम् । क्वणदलिकुलनूपुरा निरासे नलिनवनेषु पदं वसन्तलक्ष्मीः ॥

meaning_english: The Splendor of Spring, personified as a woman desiring to enter the flowering mountain forests, leaned on a sprouting mango branch. With humming swarms of bees as her anklets, she placed her foot in the lotus groves.

content_sanskrit: विकसितकुसुमाधरं हसन्तीं कुरबकराजिवधूं विलोकयन्तम् । ददृशुरिव सुराङ्गना निषण्णं सशरमनङ्गमशोकपल्लवेषु ॥
padaccheda: विकसितकुसुमाधरम् । हसन्तीं । कुरबकराजिवधूं । विलोकयन्तम् । ददृशुः । इव । सुराङ्गनाः । निषण्णम् । सशरम् । अनङ्गम् । अशोकपल्लवेषु

meaning_english: The celestial women saw Arjuna as if he were the god of love (Kama) himself, seated with his arrow among the Ashoka sprouts. This Kama-like figure was gazing at the 'bride' of the Kurabaka flower row, who seemed to be laughing with her blossomed-flower lips.

content_sanskrit: मुहुरनुपतता विधूयमानं विरचितसंहति दक्षिणानिलेन । अलिकुलमलकाकृतिं प्रपेदे नलिनमुखान्तविसर्पि पङ्कजिन्याः ॥
padaccheda: मुहुः । अनुपतता । विधूयमानम् । विरचितसंहति । दक्षिणानिलेन । अलिकुलम् । अलकाकृतिम् । प्रपेदे । नलिनमुखान्तविसर्पि । पङ्कजिन्याः

meaning_english: A swarm of bees, spreading over the face of a lotus, was repeatedly followed and shaken by the southern breeze. Being thus arranged into a compact mass, it took on the appearance of a lock of curly hair on the lotus-face.

content_sanskrit: श्वसनचलितपल्लवाधरोष्ठे नवनिहितेर्ष्यमिवावधूनयन्ती । मधुसुरभिणि षट्पदेन पुष्पे मुख इव शाललतावधूश्चुचुम्बे ॥

anvaya: शाललतावधूः षट्पदेन मधुसुरभिणि श्वसनचलितपल्लवाधरोष्ठे पुष्पे मुखे इव स्थिते सति, नवनिहिताम् ईर्ष्यम् अवधूनयन्ती इव चुचुम्बे।
meaning_english: A bee kissed a flower of the Shala creeper, which was personified as a bride. The flower, fragrant with honey, was like a face whose sprout-like lower lip trembled in the breeze. The creeper-bride, as if shaking off newly-arisen jealousy, was kissed by the bee on its flower-face.

content_sanskrit: प्रभवति न तदा परो विजेतुं भवति जितेन्द्रियता यदात्मरक्षा । अवजितभुवनस्तथा हि लेभे सिततुरगे विजयं न पुष्पमासः ॥

meaning_english: When control over the senses becomes one's self-defense, an enemy is not able to conquer. Indeed, for this reason, the Spring season, which conquers the whole world, could not gain victory over Arjuna, the one with white horses.

content_sanskrit: कथमिव तव संमतिर्भवित्री समम् ऋतुभिर्मुनिनावधीरितस्य । इति विरचितमल्लिकाविकासः स्मयत इव स्म मधुं निदाघकालः ॥

meaning_english: The summer season, having made the jasmine flowers bloom, seemed to smile at the spring season, saying: 'You have been disregarded by the sage (Arjuna); how then can you have an accord with the other seasons?'

content_sanskrit: बलवदपि बलं मिथोविरोधि प्रभवति नैव विपक्षनिर्जयाय । भुवनपरिभवी न यत्तदानीं तम् ऋतुगणः क्षणमुन्मनीचकार ॥

meaning_english: A force, even if strong, is not capable of conquering an enemy if its parts are mutually hostile. It is for this reason that the group of seasons, though conquerors of the world, could not for a moment agitate him (Arjuna).

content_sanskrit: श्रुतिसुखमुपवीणितं सहायैरविरललाञ्छनहारिणश्च कालाः । अविहितहरिसूनुविक्रियाणि त्रिदशवधूषु मनोभवं वितेनुः ॥

meaning_english: The music, played pleasingly on the Vina by the Gandharvas, and the seasons, charming with their distinct features, failed to cause any emotional change in Arjuna. However, they did produce feelings of love in the celestial women who were watching.

content_sanskrit: न दलति निचये तथोत्पलानां न च विषमच्छदगुच्छयूथिकासु । अभिरतुमुपलेभिरे यथासां हरितनयावयवेषु लोचनानि ॥

meaning_english: The eyes of the celestial women did not find as much delight in the clusters of blue lotuses or in the bunches of jasmine as they found in gazing upon the limbs of Arjuna, the son of Hari (Indra).

content_sanskrit: मुनिमभिमुखतां निनीषवो याः समुपययुः कमनीयतागुणेन । मदनमुपदधे स एव तासां दुरधिगमा हि गतिः प्रयोजनानाम् ॥

meaning_english: Those celestial women who, by the quality of their loveliness, approached the sage (Arjuna) desiring to win his attention, found that he himself instead produced love in them. Indeed, the outcome of undertakings is difficult to comprehend.

content_sanskrit: प्रकृतमनुससार नाभिनेयं प्रविकसदङ्गुलि पाणिपल्लवं वा । प्रथममुपहितं विलासि चक्षुः सिततुरगे न चचाल नर्तकीनाम् ॥

meaning_english: Neither the sprout-like hands with their expressive fingers, nor the theme to be enacted, were followed. The playful eyes of the dancing Apsaras, once they were first set upon Arjuna, did not waver from him.

content_sanskrit: अभिनयमनसः सुराङ्गनाया निहितमलक्तकवर्तनाभिताम्रम् । चरणमभिपपात षट्पदाली धुतनवलोहितपङ्कजाभिशङ्का ॥

meaning_english: A swarm of bees, mistaking it for a freshly shaken red lotus, flew towards the foot of a celestial nymph. Her foot was reddish from the application of lac dye, and her mind was supposed to be on her dance performance.

content_sanskrit: अविरलमलसेषु नर्तकीनां द्रुतपरिषिक्तमलक्तकं पदेषु । सवपुषामिव चित्तरागमूहुर्नमितशिखानि कदम्बकेसराणि ॥

meaning_english: The filaments of Kadamba flowers, with their tips bent, fell upon the languid feet of the dancing girls. There, they clung to the freshly applied red lac dye, appearing as if they were the embodied passion of the nymphs' hearts made visible.

content_sanskrit: नृपसुतमभितः समन्मथायाः परिजनगात्रतिरोहिताङ्गयष्टेः । स्फुटमभिलषितं बभूव वध्वा वदति हि संवृतिरेव कामितानि ॥

meaning_english: The desire of a certain love-struck woman, who tried to conceal her slender form behind her attendants while looking towards the prince, became obvious. For indeed, the very act of concealment reveals one's desires.

content_sanskrit: अभिमुनि सहसा हृते परस्या घनमरुता जघनांशुकैकदेशे । चकितमवसनोरु सत्रपायाः प्रतियुवतीरपि विस्मयं निनाय ॥

meaning_english: As one woman looked towards the sage, a strong wind suddenly carried away a part of the garment covering her hips. The sight of the bashful woman's startled, uncovered thigh caused astonishment even in her rival nymphs.

content_sanskrit: धृतबिसवलये निधाय पाणौ मुखमधिरूषितपाण्डुगण्डलेखम् । नृपसुतमपरा स्मराभितापादमधुमदालसलोचनं निदध्यौ ॥

meaning_english: Another woman, tormented by love, rested her face, whose cheeks had grown pale, upon her hand which wore a lotus-stalk bracelet. She then gazed intently at the prince, her eyes languid not from the intoxication of wine, but from passion.

content_sanskrit: सखि दयितमिहानयेति सा मां प्रहितवती कुसुमेषुणाभितप्ता । हृदयमहृदया न नाम पूर्वं भवदुपकण्ठमुपागतं विवेद ॥

meaning_english: A messenger-nymph speaks to Arjuna: "'O friend, bring my beloved here!' — saying this, she, tormented by the god of love, sent me to you. That heartless one, indeed, did not know that her own heart had already arrived in your presence."

content_sanskrit: चिरमपि कलितान्यपारयन्त्या परिगदितुं परिशुष्यता मुखेन । गतघृण गमितानि सत्सखीनां नयनयुगैः सममार्द्रतां मनांसि ॥
padaccheda: चिरम् । अपि । कलितानि । अपारयन्त्या । परिगदितुम् । परिशुष्यता । मुखेन । गतघृण । गमितानि । सत्सखीनाम् । नयनयुगैः । समम् । आर्द्रताम् । मनांसि

meaning_english: The messenger continues, addressing Arjuna: 'O pitiless one! Unable to speak the words she had conceived for so long, her face drying up, she caused the minds of her good friends to become moist with compassion, along with their eyes which filled with tears.'

content_sanskrit: अचकमत सपल्लवां धरित्रीं मृदुसुरभिं विरहय्य पुष्पशय्याम् । भृशमरतिमवाप्य तत्र चास्यास्तव सुखशीतमुपैतुमङ्कमिच्छा ॥
padaccheda: अचकमत । सपल्लवाम् । धरित्रीम् । मृदुसुरभिम् । विरहय्य । पुष्पशय्याम् । भृशम् । अरतिम् । अवाप्य । तत्र । च । अस्याः । तव । सुखशीतम् । उपैतुम् । अङ्कम् । इच्छा

meaning_english: Her desire made her prefer the earth with its fresh sprouts, having abandoned the soft, fragrant flower-bed. And having become extremely restless there, she wishes to attain your pleasantly cool lap.

content_sanskrit: तदनघ तनुरस्तु सा सकामा व्रजति पुरा हि परासुतां त्वदर्थे । पुनरपि सुलभं तपोऽनुरागी युवतिजनः खलु नाप्यतेऽनुरूपः ॥
padaccheda: तत् । अनघ । तनुः । अस्तु । सा । सकामा । व्रजति । पुरा । हि । परासुताम् । त्वदर्थे । पुनः । अपि । सुलभम् । तपः । अनुरागी । युवतिजनः । खलु । न । आप्यते । अनुरूपः
anvaya: अनघ, तत् सा तनुः सकामा अस्तु । हि (सा) त्वदर्थे पुरा परासुतां व्रजति । तपः पुनः अपि सुलभम्, (किन्तु) अनुरूपः अनुरागी युवतिजनः खलु न आप्यते ।
meaning_english: O sinless one, therefore let that body of hers have its desire fulfilled, for she is about to die for your sake. Penance can be easily undertaken again, but a suitable, affectionate young woman is indeed not to be found.

content_sanskrit: जहिहि कठिनतां प्रयच्छ वाचं ननु करुणामृदु मानसं मुनीनाम् । उपगतमवधीरयन्त्यभव्याः स निपुणमेत्य कयाचिदेवमूचे ॥
padaccheda: जहिहि । कठिनताम् । प्रयच्छ । वाचम् । ननु । करुणामृदु । मानसम् । मुनीनाम् । उपगतम् । अवधीरयन्ति । अभव्याः । सः । निपुणम् । एत्य । कयाचित् । एवम् । ऊचे
anvaya: (हे मुने) कठिनतां जहिहि, वाचं प्रयच्छ । ननु मुनीनां मानसं करुणा-मृदु (भवति) । अभव्याः उपगतम् अवधीरयन्ति । सः कयाचित् निपुणम् एत्य एवम् ऊचे ।
meaning_english: "Abandon your hardness, speak. Surely, the minds of sages are soft with compassion. It is the unfortunate who disregard one who has approached." Having skillfully approached, he (Arjuna) was thus addressed by a certain woman.

content_sanskrit: सललितचलितत्रिकाभिरामाः शिरसिजसंयमनाकुलैकपाणिः । सुरपतितनयेऽपरा निरासे मनसिजजैत्रशरं विलोचनार्धम् ॥
padaccheda: सललितचलितत्रिकाभिरामाः । शिरसिजसंयमनाकुलैकपाणिः । सुरपतितनये । अपरा । निरासे । मनसिजजैत्रशरम् । विलोचनार्धम्
anvaya: अपरा, सललित-चलित-त्रिक-अभिरामा, शिरसिज-संयमन-आकुल-एकपाणिः (सती), सुरपतितनये मनसिज-जैत्र-शरं विलोचन-अर्धं निरासे ।
meaning_english: Another woman, charming with her gracefully moving lower back and with one hand occupied in tying up her hair, cast upon Arjuna, the son of Indra, a half-glance, which was like a conquering arrow of the god of love.

content_sanskrit: कुसुमितमवलम्ब्य चूतमुच्चैस्तनुरिभकुम्भपृथुस्तनानताङ्गी । तदभिमुखमनङ्गचापयष्टिर्विसृतगुणेव समुन्ननाम काचित् ॥
padaccheda: कुसुमितम् । अवलम्ब्य । चूतम् । उच्चैः । तनुः । इभकुम्भपृथुस्तनानताङ्गी । तदभिमुखम् । अनङ्गचापयष्टिः । विसृतगुणा । इव । समुन्ननाम । काचित्
anvaya: काचित् इभ-कुम्भ-पृथु-स्तन-अनत-अङ्गी तनुः, कुसुमितं चूतम् अवलम्ब्य, विसृत-गुणा अनङ्ग-चाप-यष्टिः इव, उच्चैः तत्-अभिमुखं समुन्ननाम ।
meaning_english: A certain slender woman, whose body was bent by her breasts as large as the frontal globes of an elephant, held onto a flowering mango tree and arched her body high towards him, like the bow of Kamadeva being strung.

content_sanskrit: सरभसमवलम्ब्य नीलमन्या विगलितनीवि विलोलमन्तरीयम् । अभिपतितुमनाः ससाध्वसेव च्युतरशनागुणसंदितावतस्थे ॥
padaccheda: सरभसम् । अवलम्ब्य । नीलम् । अन्या । विगलितनीवि । विलोलम् । अन्तरीयम् । अभिपतितुमनाः । ससाध्वसा । इव । च्युतरशनागुणसंदिता । अवतस्थे
anvaya: अन्या, विगलित-नीवि विलोलम् अन्तरीयं सरभसम् अवलम्ब्य, अभिपतितु-मनाः, ससाध्वसा इव, च्युत-रशना-गुणेन संदिता (सती) अवतस्थे ।
meaning_english: Another woman, hastily holding her fluttering blue lower garment whose knot had come undone, stood still as if with fear, with a mind to rush towards him, her garment held together only by the fallen girdle-string.

content_sanskrit: यदि मनसि शमः किमङ्ग चापं शठ विषयास्तव वल्लभा न मुक्तिः । भवतु दिशति नान्यकामिनीभ्यस्तव हृदये हृदयेश्वरावकाशम् ॥
padaccheda: यदि । मनसि । शमः । किम् । अङ्ग । चापम् । शठ । विषयाः । तव । वल्लभाः । न । मुक्तिः । भवतु । दिशति । न । अन्यकामिनीभ्यः । तव । हृदये । हृदयेश्वरः । अवकाशम्
anvaya: अङ्ग शठ, यदि मनसि शमः (अस्ति), (तर्हि) चापं किम्? तव विषयाः वल्लभाः, मुक्तिः न । भवतु, हृदयेश्वरः तव हृदये अन्य-कामिनीभ्यः अवकाशं न दिशति ।
meaning_english: "O deceitful one, if there is tranquility in your mind, why the bow? Sensual objects are dear to you, not liberation. So be it! The lord of hearts (Kamadeva) gives no space in your heart to other women (besides us)."

content_sanskrit: इति विषमितचक्षुषाभिधाय स्फुरदधरोष्ठमसूयया कयाचित् । अगणितगुरुमानलज्जयासौ स्वयमुरसि श्रवणोत्पलेन जघ्ने ॥
padaccheda: इति । विषमितचक्षुषा । अभिधाय । स्फुरदधरोष्ठम् । असूयया । कयाचित् । अगणितगुरुमानलज्जया । असौ । स्वयम् । उरसि । श्रवणोत्पलेन । जघ्ने
anvaya: इति असूयया विषमित-चक्षुषा स्फुरत्-अधर-ओष्ठम् अभिधाय, कयाचित् अगणित-गुरु-मान-लज्जया असौ स्वयम् उरसि श्रवण-उत्पलेन जघ्ने ।
meaning_english: Having spoken thus with a jealous, sidelong glance that made her lower lip throb, he (Arjuna) was struck on the chest with a lotus from her ear by a certain woman who had cast aside all regard for elders, pride, and shame.

content_sanskrit: सविनयमपराभिसृत्य साचि स्मितसुभगैकलसत्कपोललक्ष्मीः । श्रवणनियमितेन तं निदध्य सकलमिवासकलेन लोचनेन ॥
padaccheda: सविनयम् । अपरा । अभिसृत्य । साचि । स्मितसुभगैकलसत्कपोललक्ष्मीः । श्रवणनियमितेन । तम् । निदध्यौ । सकलम् । इव । असकलेन । लोचनेन
anvaya: अपरा, स्मित-सुभग-एक-लसत्-कपोल-लक्ष्मीः (सती), सविनयं साचि अभिसृत्य, श्रवण-नियमितेन असकलेन लोचनेन तम् सकलम् इव निदध्यौ ।
meaning_english: Another woman, whose beauty resided on one cheek made charming by a smile, modestly approached him obliquely and gazed at him with her partial eye drawn back towards her ear, as if she were seeing him completely with it.

content_sanskrit: करुणमभिहितं त्रपा निरस्ता तदभिमुखं च विमुक्तमश्रु ताभिः । प्रकुपितमभिसारणेऽनुनेतुं प्रियमियती ह्यबलाजनस्य भूमिः ॥
padaccheda: करुणम् । अभिहितम् । त्रपा । निरस्ता । तदभिमुखम् । च । विमुक्तम् । अश्रु । ताभिः । प्रकुपितम् । अभिसारणे । अनुनेतुम् । प्रियम् । इयती । हि । अबलाजनस्य । भूमिः
anvaya: ताभिः करुणम् अभिहितम्, त्रपा निरस्ता, तत्-अभिमुखं च अश्रु विमुक्तम् । हि अभिसारणे प्रकुपितं प्रियम् अनुनेतुं अबला-जनस्य इयती भूमिः (अस्ति) ।
meaning_english: Piteous words were spoken by them, shame was cast aside, and tears were shed towards him. Indeed, this is the extent of a woman's power to appease an angered beloved during a tryst.

content_sanskrit: असकलनयनेक्षितानि लज्जा गतमलसं परिपाण्डुता विषादः । इति विविधमियाय तासु भूषां प्रभवति मण्डयितुं वधूरनङ्गः ॥
padaccheda: असकलनयनेक्षितानि । लज्जा । गतम् । अलसम् । परिपाण्डुता । विषादः । इति । विविधम् । इयाय । तासु । भूषाम् । प्रभवति । मण्डयितुम् । वधूः । अनङ्गः
anvaya: लज्जा असकल-नयन-ईक्षितानि, विषादः परिपाण्डुता, अलसं गतम्, इति विविधं तासु भूषाम् इयाय । अनङ्गः वधूः मण्डयितुं प्रभवति ।
meaning_english: Shyness became their sidelong glances, despondency became their paleness, and their gait became languid. Thus, in various ways, these states became ornaments for them. Kamadeva is indeed able to adorn women.

content_sanskrit: अलसपदमनोरमं प्रकृत्या जितकलहंसवधूगति प्रयातम् । स्थितमुरुजघनस्थलातिभारादुदितपरिश्रमजिह्मितेक्षणं वा ॥
padaccheda: अलसपदमनोरमम् । प्रकृत्या । जितकलहंसवधूगति । प्रयातम् । स्थितम् । उरुजघनस्थलातिभारात् । उदितपरिश्रमजिह्मितेक्षणम् । वा
anvaya: प्रकृत्या अलस-पद-मनोरमं जित-कलहंस-वधू-गति प्रयातम्, वा उरु-जघन-स्थल-अतिभारात् उदित-परिश्रम-जिह्मित-ईक्षणं स्थितम् (तासु भूषाम् इयाय) ।
meaning_english: Their walking, naturally charming with languid steps and surpassing the gait of a female swan, or their standing posture, with eyes drooping from the fatigue caused by the weight of their ample hips, also became their adornments.

content_sanskrit: भृशकुसुमशरेषुपातमोहादनवसितार्थपदाकुलोऽभिलापः । अधिकविततलोचनं वधूनामयुगपदुन्नमितभ्रु वीक्षितं च ॥
padaccheda: भृशकुसुमशरेषुपातमोहात् । अनवसितार्थपदाकुलः । अभिलापः । अधिकविततलोचनम् । वधूनाम् । अयुगपदुन्नमितभ्रु । वीक्षितम् । च
anvaya: वधूनां भृश-कुसुम-शर-इषु-पात-मोहात् अनवसित-अर्थ-पद-आकुलः अभिलापः, च अधिक-वितत-लोचनम् अयुगपत्-उन्नमित-भ्रु वीक्षितं (भूषाम् इयाय) ।
meaning_english: The women's speech, confused with incomplete but meaningful words due to the delusion caused by the intense shower of Kamadeva's arrows, and their glances, with eyes wide open and one eyebrow raised, also became their adornments.

content_sanskrit: रुचिकरमपि नार्थवद्बभूव स्तिमितसमाधिशुचौ पृथातनूजे । ज्वलयति महतां मनांस्यमर्षे न हि लभतेऽवसरं सुखाभिलाषः ॥
padaccheda: रुचिकरम् । अपि । न । अर्थवत् । बभूव । स्तिमितसमाधिशुचौ । पृथातनूजे । ज्वलयति । महताम् । मनांसि । अमर्षे । न । हि । लभते । अवसरम् । सुखाभिलाषः
anvaya: (तत् सर्वं) रुचिकरम् अपि स्तिमित-समाधि-शुचौ पृथा-तनूजे अर्थवत् न बभूव । हि अमर्षे महतां मनांसि ज्वलयति (सति), सुख-अभिलाषः अवसरं न लभते ।
meaning_english: Even though all this was charming, it had no effect on the son of Pritha, who was pure due to his steady meditation. For when indignation burns the minds of the great, the desire for pleasure finds no opportunity.

content_sanskrit: स्वयं संराध्यैवं शतमखमखण्डेन तपसा परोच्छित्त्या लभ्यामभिलषति लक्ष्मीं हरिसुते । मनोभिः सोद्वेगैः प्रणयविहतैध्वस्तरुचयः सगन्धर्मा धाम त्रिदशवनिताः स्वं प्रतिययुः ॥
padaccheda: स्वयम् । संराध्य । एवम् । शतमखम् । अखण्डेन । तपसा । परोच्छित्त्या । लभ्याम् । अभिलषति । लक्ष्मीम् । हरिसुते । मनोभिः । सोद्वेगैः । प्रणयविहतैः । ध्वस्तरुचयः । सगन्धर्वाः । धाम । त्रिदशवनिताः । स्वम् । प्रतिययुः
anvaya: हरिसुते एवम् अखण्डेन तपसा स्वयम् शतमखं संराध्य पर-उच्छित्त्या लभ्यां लक्ष्मीम् अभिलषति (सति), स-गन्धर्वाः त्रिदश-वनिताः प्रणय-विहतैः स-उद्वेगैः मनोभिः ध्वस्त-रुचयः (सत्यः) स्वं धाम प्रतिययुः ।
meaning_english: While Arjuna, son of Indra, thus desired the glory obtainable by destroying his enemies after propitiating Indra himself with unbroken penance, the celestial women, along with the Gandharvas, their charm gone and their minds agitated and frustrated in love, returned to their own abode.
